memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not steal. Do not lie. Do not deceive one another. Do not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 19:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four short commands, and none of them dramatic. Do not steal. Do not lie. Do not deceive. Do not misuse God's name.

These are the everyday sins — the ones respectable people commit without ever feeling like sinners. Taking small things from work that no one will miss. The convenient version of a story that makes us look better. The promise made with no intention of keeping it.

Notice the third one especially: do not deceive one another. That goes beyond outright lies. It covers the technically true statement designed to mislead. The important detail left out. The impression created that we know is false.

And notice who this is about. One another. These are sins against the people around us — colleagues, customers, neighbours, family.

Then comes the sharpest phrase: and so profane the name of your God. When we deceive, we say something false about the God we claim to serve. The world does not read our theology. It reads our conduct.

Paul writes: each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbour, for we are all members of one body (Eph 4:25).

Truthfulness is not a small virtue. It is how a community holds together.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you created a false impression without technically lying?
2. What "small" dishonesty have you stopped noticing in yourself?
3. Does your everyday conduct match the God you claim to serve?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me honest in the small things where nobody checks. Let my conduct speak truthfully about the God I belong to. Amen.
